::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 13 th [1872]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels
:::

My dear [Christabel](people/person_329.qmd)
York and Lancaster Rose has gone- one half to school- and the other has grown too busy, so it resigns, and I have accepted a 

[Miss Alice Poole](people/person_1188.qmd)[^1]
Uffington
Farrington

She is sister to [a governess](people/person_1187.qmd) I like very much –

[Hanbury Mills](other_books/otherbook_829.qmd) was an immense pleasure to [Gertrude](people/person_1462.qmd).  She and [Frances](people/person_1604.qmd) have both bought one.  I think Linda is true, but as you say, it was not possible to bring her out more.  I confess I had rather not have married Frank  I think he got restless and picked his moustaches, and frightened her.  I doubt too whether Patty would have come off with such flying colours with old Mr Weatherby

your affectionate
Mother Goose

[The lady with a long nose](other_books/otherbook_831.qmd) will end in the summer. Then we will have your [Face](other_books/otherbook_437.qmd) if it is not too ghastly for a serial

---

[^1]: 'York and Lancaster Rose' was the sobriquet of two sisters, members of the [Gosling Society](organizations/other_104.qmd).  Their replacement, Alice F. S. Poole (b. Newland, Gloucestershire 1849/50), was living at Uffington with her mother Catherine Poole (b. 1807/8);  she later became a governess and at the time of the 1881 census was living in Camberwell with her sister Harriet Poole (b. Mansfield, Nottingham 1843/4), also a governess.  The latter is probably the Miss Poole to whom there are several other references.
